conviction_note: The run-rate arithmetic points to a small total-revenue beat and a likely raise to the product guide: H1 product was $464M against an $850-950M FY guide, and Q2 alone ran at $239M. But this name sold its last beat-and-raise for -9.9%. The stock also carries a near-certain GAAP EPS hit from the ST-920 IPR&D charge and a weak hint that the US start-form cadence slowed. So p_up is only 55, on a 10% absolute move (the median reaction is 9.6%; the option chain is unusable). Scaled: (2*0.55-1)*10 = +1.0, against a findings sum of +0.8; the two agree in sign and size.
bar: Q3 2026 total revenue consensus about $305M: Yahoo average $305.01M from 14 analysts, range $273.7-322.1M (https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/PTCT/analysis/). Benzinga, via search snippet, shows $304.4-309.6M (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/PTCT/earnings-forecasts). EPS consensus $0.30 from only 3 analysts, range $0.24-0.36. Company guide (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001070081/000107008126000016/tmb-20260728xex99d1.htm): FY26 product revenue $850-950M (raised from $750-850M), total revenue $1.18-1.28B. H1 product was $464.4M (Q1 $225.6M, Q2 $238.8M), so the guide implies H2 product of $386-486M, or $193-243M a quarter. Q2 total of $361M included a $50M Novartis milestone, so Q3's bar has no milestone in it. My estimate for Q3 total is about $305-325M: product about $235-255M, Evrysdi royalty about $70-75M.
positioning_check: Short interest on the 2026-10-15 record date: 8.30M shares, 10.51% of float, 7.6 days to cover, down 9.4% from 9.17M at the prior settlement (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/PTCT/short-interest, FINRA data published 2026-10-26). Moderately crowded and covering. Skew is not available: chain status unusable_chain, ATM spread 83% of mid, put/call OI ratio 1.0. The stock sits 28.6% below its 52-week high and 8% above its 52-week low; 20-day run-up -0.27%, 5-day +1.46%. The prior eight reactions were 6 up and 2 down, median absolute move 9.58%.

findings.finding: The run-rate math puts Q3 product revenue above what the FY guide implies, so a raise is likely. H1 product was $464.4M; the $850-950M guide implies $193-243M a quarter in H2. Q2 product was already $238.8M, with Sephience at $151.3M (+21% q/q, after +36% in Q1). Commercial patients rose from 1,244 to 1,647 in Q2 (+403, against +298 in Q1). Another +15-20% q/q in Sephience (about $175-180M) would put Q3 product near $240-255M, at or above the top of the implied range and a few $M above the roughly $233M product line inside the $305M total consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 (product guide raised to $750-850M): +14.27%. Q2 2026 (Sephience +21% q/q, revenue beat about 23% on a $50M milestone, product guide raised to $850-950M): -9.94%. Nov 2025: +5.98%. Raises have been bought and sold about equally; the most recent one was sold.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus at $305M sits inside a guide that the Q2 run-rate already exceeds, so the street models H2 conservatively. If a raise were fully priced, the stock would not sit 28.6% below its 52-week high with 10.5% of float short after a raise, and the Q3 high estimate ($322M) would be closer to the average.
findings.independence: Q1 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001070081/000107008126000011/tmb-20260507xex99d1.htm) gives Q1 Sephience $124.6M and product $225.6M. Cantor conference summary, 2026-09-11 (https://quartr.com/events/ptc-therapeutics-inc-ptct-12th-annual-cantor-fitzgerald-global-healthcare-conference_ofWxEewK): 'launch exceeded expectations', discontinuations stabilising at 20-25%. Same company, different documents.

findings.finding: The counterparty series puts Evrysdi royalty in line. Roche's Q3 Evrysdi sales were CHF 502m (9M CHF 1,470m less H1 CHF 968m), flat on Q2's CHF 504m and up from Q1's CHF 464m. PTC booked $71.1M of Evrysdi royalty on Q2 and $46.8M on Q1; the tiered rate steps up within the year. So Q3 royalty should come in around $70-75M, about what a $305M total bar needs.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Royalty has never been the swing line in a PTCT reaction; the stock trades on Sephience and the guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Roche's 9M tables are public, so this is largely priced. It is filed because it removes a downside path for the total-revenue line, not because it adds upside.
findings.independence: Roche H1 release, 2026-07-23 (https://www.roche.com/media/releases/med-cor-2026-07-23): Evrysdi H1 CHF 968m. Roche Q1 release, 2026-04-23 (https://www.roche.com/media/releases/med-cor-2026-04-23): CHF 464m. Same issuer, separate documents.

findings.finding: PTC closed the ST-920 (Sangamo Fabry gene therapy) acquisition on 2026-09-21, inside Q3, for $111M upfront. For a BLA-stage asset this is normally expensed as acquired IPR&D, which would be about $1.3-1.4 per share against a $0.30 EPS consensus that only 3 analysts publish. GAAP EPS would then print as a loss, a headline 'miss' that is non-recurring.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 2025 EPS was -$1.80 against -$0.41 consensus (Yahoo history); the 2026-02-19 reaction was +1.09%, so an EPS headline miss was looked through then.
findings.why_not_priced: Only 3 of the 14 analysts carry an EPS estimate, and the $0.24-0.36 range suggests most have not booked the charge. Headline algos read GAAP EPS. If it were priced, the EPS consensus would be negative.
findings.independence: Deal terms in the 2026-08-12 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1070081/000110465926095424/tmb-20260812xex99d1.htm): $111M upfront, closing late Q3 or early Q4, no effect on the 2026 cash-flow-breakeven goal. Same company.

findings.finding: The Q2 release dropped the US start-form cadence. The Q1 release gave about 140 start forms a month and more than 1,500 cumulative; Q4 2025 gave 1,134. The Q2 release gives only patients on therapy. The Cantor summary of 2026-09-11 says 'over 2,000' US start forms; 140 a month from about 1,520 at March 31 would be about 2,270 by mid-September. This weakly suggests new US starts slowed in Q2-Q3. It is a proxy, and growing ex-US revenue (US is 'the majority') partly offsets it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 print (+21% q/q, slower than Q1's +36%) was sold -9.94%. The market appears to trade on the Sephience growth rate.
findings.why_not_priced: Nobody aggregates a metric a company stopped disclosing. If it were priced, the Q3 consensus would sit lower than a figure that already implies about 15% q/q Sephience growth.
findings.independence: Cantor conference summary (https://quartr.com/events/ptc-therapeutics-inc-ptct-12th-annual-cantor-fitzgerald-global-healthcare-conference_ofWxEewK, 2026-09-11) is an AI-generated secondary summary, and '2,000+' is a floor, not a count. Shares its premise with finding 1 but points the other way; net of each other the two give the Sephience read.

findings.finding: Votoplam: in the Q2 release PTC and Novartis said they would engage the FDA in 2H 2026 on the 24-month PIVOT-HD data (10 mg dose: about 52% slowing against natural history) and possible accelerated pathways. Phase 3 INVEST-HD (about 770 patients, readout 2030) is the stated base case. The Q3 call is the first natural place to report FDA feedback, and it could cut either way.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 24-month data release (April 2026) moved the stock about -6% on the lack of statistical significance (rallies.ai, undated).
findings.why_not_priced: BioSpace reads the Phase 3 start as doubt about accelerated approval, so the market expects no accelerated path. Any opening would be upside to a low bar; a clear 'no' is largely already the base case.
findings.independence: BioSpace (https://www.biospace.com/drug-development/novartis-ptc-push-huntingtons-drug-into-phase-3-mum-on-accelerated-approval): analysts read the Phase 3 start as apprehension about accelerated approval.

findings.why_not_priced: Short interest is public, but a squeeze needs the print to trigger it. The shorts are already covering slowly, so part of this is unwinding.
findings.independence: Equibles history (https://equibles.com/stocks/ptct/short-interest): 10.24M shares short and 5.99 days to cover in mid-May 2026, so the short has eased since spring.

baseline_tension: No skew is available. A modest positive lean from run-rate arithmetic runs into the name's recent habit of selling a beat-and-raise (-9.9% in July) and a 28.6% drawdown from the high; moderate short interest cuts both ways.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): the guidance/run-rate finding cut from +1.5 to +1.0, because the last beat-and-raise was sold -9.9%.
Lesson 2 (one-offs): the ST-920 IPR&D EPS hit cut from -0.5 to -0.4; it is non-recurring, sits below the revenue line the stock trades on, and a Q4 2025 EPS miss was looked through.
Lessons 5 and 9 (proxy; net of segment): the start-form disclosure inference cut from -0.7 to -0.5; it is a secondary-summary proxy and ex-US growth offsets it.
Lesson 6 (inside the guide): Translarna/Emflaza cut from -0.3 to -0.2; it lands inside an already-raised guide.
Lesson 7: short interest looked up before the negatives (10.5% of float, 7.6 days to cover); handled through the positioning finding, not by shrinking the negatives twice.
